root.name: Modern Defense: Pterodactyl Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 g6 3. d4 Bg7 4. Nc3 Qa5

overview: Black plays ...Qa5 early against the Open Sicilian-style Nc3 set-up, with the g7 bishop on the long diagonal and ...Qxc3-style tricks against the d4 pawn. White usually answers with Bd2 or Bb5+, or plays Nxc5-style captures and builds a centre. Play is tricky and manoeuvring with Black counter-punching against the e4 and c3 squares.

white_ideas.idea: Build the e4/d4 centre with Bd2 or Bb5+ and chase the queen
Castle and push with f4 or Bg5 against a loose Black set-up

black_ideas.idea: Pressure e4 and c3 with the queen and bishop, then play ...cxd4 and ...Nf6
Use the long diagonal to hit d4 and c3

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-like asymmetry with Black c-pawn trade and fianchettoed bishop
White centre against Black queen on a5

character.notes: Tricky but not forcing; the queen sortie gives tactical chances.

gambit.notes: No material is given if White plays accurately.

soundness.notes: Considered sound but a little loosening; White can get an edge.

structure.notes: The d-pawn trades for the c-pawn, leaving a half-open c-file.

level.notes: Tricks need care but little to memorise.

sublines_that_differ.name: Modern Pterodactyl move order
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. Nf3 Qa5
sublines_that_differ.how: Same idea via the Modern; the most played route to this position.

character.reason: It is tricky rather than forcing and White can steer toward calm development.

gambit.reason: No material is offered; the early queen raid is positional.

soundness.reason: White can get a small edge but the line is playable.

structure.reason: The c-pawn trades for the d-pawn as in the Sicilian, giving a half-open file.

level.reason: The plans need care but there is little long theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White occupy the centre and strikes from the g7 bishop and queen.
